newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analysts' comments on Philips Q1 results.
newsitem.headline: Analysts' comments on Philips Q1 results.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV on Wednesday reported first quarter net profits from ordinary operations rose to 460 million guilders from 377 million.

Total net income for the group rose to 887 million guilders from 692 million, boosted by a 427 million guilder extraordinary gain which was mainly due to the partial flotation of Philips' stake in ASM Lithography
Below is a collection of analysts' comments on the results:

"We are extremely pleased with this result and the progress that has been booked in this first quarter. We are happy with the improvement at consumer products, but actually also across the board. Of course the deconsolidation of (German consumer products unit) Grundig and (U.S. vacuum cleaner manufacturer) Regina (sold last December) helped consumer products. But the other units also performed in line with our expectations. We had been forecasting net from normal operations of 453 million guilders, so we are very happy."

"Looking simply at the figures, it's good: they're up. Looking deeper, the main problem is that everything is rather slack. We had expected semiconductors to do better: in fact, they're lower. The big thing is that Grundig is out which has helped consumer products. I'm a bit disappointed. In the next half, we expect semiconductors to pick up and deconsolidation to help. We had Philips as a Hold and we will probably keep it there."

"It was an extremely good quarter for consumer products. The quarter was also strong in other areas with a nice margin recovery at lighting. Margins for components and semiconductors went down year on year, but were up from quarter to quarter. One striking element on the negative side is the poor combination of Origin and Philips Media: taking out Polygram, there's still a net loss. Margin development in Asia is also down. The outlook for the company is surprisingly good: we're expecting to see the impact of restructurings in the next quarters."
